evidence.observed_result: Fresh M02 objectives created appropriate to confidentiality: explain privacy vs confidentiality everyday language, describe informed consent and how shown, give boundary examples inside/outside role, explain role-dependent disclosure duties (when must share/when must not, why depends on role/setting/consent), list practical steps for family/coworker/social-media requests, support sensitive disclosure while staying in role and clear about limits, find official help in NY and federal. Fresh scenarios: Sam/Elena Bronx wellness center private disclosure not permission for sister/coworker; sister 'I'm emergency contact' call — explain emergency contact ≠ automatic sharing; coworker 'forward Elena intake for address/flyers' — minimum necessary; social media friend request + gift $40 — agency $15 limit + personal/work separation; 10-year-old overnight mandated reporting example under SSL §413. All everyday language, not legal advice.

Explained privacy as person's right to control who sees story (person holding door) and confidentiality as receiver's duty to protect and share only when appropriate (what you do inside door). Consent as clear information + understanding + voluntary agreement without pressure, with what/with whom/purpose/how long/yes-no/revocable elements [M02-1][M02-2]. Boundaries as agreed predictable limits keeping relationship respectful/fair/safe — time/place, role (peer specialist not diagnosis/prescribing/lending money), gifts/money, social media/personal contact, self-disclosure — example 'I keep work and personal social media separate to protect your privacy and my role' [M02-7][M02-9]. Role-dependent duties: must NOT share without permission with family/friends/outside coworkers [M02-1][M02-3][M02-4]; must consider mandated reporting SSL §413 reasonable cause threshold to Statewide Central Register 1-800-342-3009 via nysmandatedreporter.org [M02-5]; imminent risk requires immediate supervisor/clinical lead assessment least-necessary sharing agency safety plan [M02-4][M02-8]; Part 2 stricter than HIPAA [M02-2]. All plain language with role examples.

Created fresh source identifiers [M02-1]–[M02-16] appropriate to M02 with accurate classifications: [M02-1] HHS HIPAA Privacy Rule hhs.gov official; [M02-2] SAMHSA+eCFR 42 CFR Part 2 official + govinfo; [M02-3] NYS DOH PHL §18 official health.ny.gov + statute text via Cornell LII nysenate nongovernmental publisher labeled; [M02-4] NYS OMH MHL §33.13 official omh.ny.gov + nysenate; [M02-5] NYS OCFS/Justice Center SSL §413 official ocfs.ny.gov + mandated reporter training; [M02-6] NYS OP Education Law §6509 official op.nysed.gov; [M02-7] NYS OMH+NYC DOHMH official; [M02-8] OMH safety/duty-to-protect official; [M02-9] NASW Code of Ethics professional association nongovernmental (not government primary); [M02-10] HHS+govinfo official regulatory repositories; [M02-11] OASAS official; [M02-12] Justice Center official; [M02-13] 42 USC §290dd-2 official govinfo; [M02-14] SAMHSA Part2 exceptions official; [M02-15] OPWDD official; [M02-16] law publisher Cornell LII nysenate nongovernmental for statutes.
